newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down at intraday low vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down at intraday low vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended down at an intraday low of 8.2961 on Monday from Friday's 8.2955 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai, mainly on speculative selling that emerged just before the close, dealers said.
The weighted average price last Friday was 8.2957.
The yuan opened up at 8.2952 and consolidated around the opening level for most the session, hitting a high of 8.2951 before it moved down.
Trading was dull with most done at 8.2953, dealers said.
"Speculative selling emerged after the yuan failed to stand above the 8.2950 level late in the session," said one dealer.
A second dealer said the central bank was seen buying the dollar despite an increase in its foreign exchange reserves.
China's foreign exchange reserves exceeded $110 billion at the end of February against $105 billion at the end of 1996, official figures showed.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to fall further on Tuesday.
The yuan closed up at 6.8100 from 6.8540 against 100 Japanese yen and down at an intraday low of 1.0723 from 1.0708 against the Hong Kong dollar.
